node.title: Re: What defines the output format of a Postgres Timestamp
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Now I'm wondering where the output format is defined.

A quick look at the documentation: sections [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/13/datatype-datetime.html#DATATYPE-DATETIME-OUTPUT|8.5.2. Date/Time Output] and [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/13/runtime-config-client.html#RUNTIME-CONFIG-CLIENT-FORMAT|19.11.2. Locale and Formatting] appear to discuss this.

I would have to change each and every select statement to have a TO_CHAR with the proper format.

[https://stackoverflow.com/a/8616252|This StackOverflow answer] suggests defining a function to curry the arguments.

In another piece of code I have lying around that uses [mod://Mojo::Pg], I use [mod://DateTime::Format::Strptime] to parse the date strings coming from Postgres and [mod://DateTime]'s strftime to format them, though I suspect that's going to be less efficient than letting the database handle it.
